post.caption: Goya's duchess wears two named rings. Goya painted the Duchess of Alba in oil on canvas. The portrait is kept in the Hispanic Society in New York. One ring is inscribed Alba and the other Goya. With her right hand, she points at the ground. In the sand are the words Solo Goya, which mean only Goya. Goya kept the painting in his studio until 1812. His son then owned it and sold it in 1836. Archer Huntington gave it to the Hispanic Society in 1907. The date written in the sand is 1797.
